REGENT OF SLEMAN

SPECIAL REGION OF YOGYAKARTA

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SLEMAN REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

heading: REGENT OF SLEMAN,
HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF SLEMAN REGENCY
translated_text:
HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF SLEMAN REGENCY

and

heading: REGENT OF SLEMAN
translated_text:
REGENT OF SLEMAN

HAS DECIDED:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.

heading: CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women are persons of female gender. 4. Children are persons who have not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb.
5. Victims are women and children who experience suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring within the territory of the Region.
6. Violence is any act against women and children that results in suffering or hardship physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
7. Women's empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after being restored and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to perform their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by persons or representatives of institutions with expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against victims will, is, and/or has occurred.
14. Services are immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree.
16. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is a technical implementing unit of the Regional Apparatus that carries out technical operational activities and/or technical supporting activities for integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
17. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is established at the Regional, sub-district, and village levels.
18. Region is Sleman Regency.
19. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
20. Regent is the Regent of Sleman.
21. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region.

heading: Article 2
translated_text:
Article 2

Protection of women and children victims of violence is implemented based on the principles of:
a. respect and recognition of rights; andb. equal human dignity.

heading: Article 3
Article 4
translated_text:
Article 4

1. The objectives of protection of women victims of violence are directed to: a. creating conditions that support the development of the potential of women victims of violence;
b. strengthening the potential already possessed by women victims of violence; andc. improving the work skills of women victims of violence.
2. The objectives of protection of children victims of violence are directed to: a. providing social rehabilitation for children victims of violence; b. reuniting children victims of violence with their families and/or environment; andc. increasing the empowerment of children victims of violence.

Article 5

a. prevention of violence against women;
b. protection services for women victims of violence; and c. empowerment of women victims of violence.

heading: Article 15
CHAPTER IV
CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 17

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to prevent violence against women and children, in the form of:a. collecting data and organizing an information system for the protection of women and children victims of violence;
b. conducting education on anti-violence values towards women and children; andc. disseminating laws and regulations related to the empowerment of women and protection of child victims of violence.
2. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for Victims in the form of: a. establishing and organizing technical service institutions for Victims by involving community elements; andb. encouraging public awareness of the importance of protection for victims of violence.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Part One

General

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

Technical service institutions for Victims are implemented by P2TP2A and FPKK.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

P2TP2A

Article 19

1. The provision of services to victims is carried out in an integrated manner by P2TP2A.
2. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in a networked manner.

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

1. P2TP2A provides services and temporary protection in the form of safe houses.
2. In the event that P2TP2A does not yet have a safe house, then victims of violence are referred to other integrated service centers that have safe houses.

heading: Article 21
Article 22
Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

FPKK

Article 23

1. In order to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence, FPKK is established.
2. FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of:a. Regional FPKK;
b. Sub-district FPKK; andc. Village FPKK.
3. The establishment of Regional FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a is determined by the Regent.
4. The establishment of Sub-district FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b is determined by the sub-district head.
5. The establishment of Village FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c is determined by the village head.
6. Further provisions regarding the organizational structure and elements of FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 24
CHAPTER VII
Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. In addition to P2TP2A as referred to in Article 20, the community may form forums/groups at the sub-district and village levels that function as P2TP2A networks in the framework of implementing efforts to protect women and children victims of violence.
2. The formation of forums/groups in villages as referred to in paragraph (1) may be facilitated by the Village Government.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

MONITORING, EVALUATION, AND REPORTING

Article 27

The implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that has duties and responsibilities in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

1. The Regional Apparatus that has duties and responsibilities in the field of women's empowerment and child protection is obligated to conduct monitoring, evaluation, and reporting of the results of activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence on a regular basis.
2. The reporting of activity results as referred to in paragraph (1) is submitted to the Regent through the Regional Apparatus that has duties and responsibilities in the field of regional development planning.
3. The implementation of monitoring, evaluation and reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) involves the forum for handling victims of violence against women and children in a tiered manner.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 29

1. Guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that has duties and responsibilities in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) include:a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; andd. monitoring and evaluation.
3. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers aspects related to planning and implementation.
4. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers aspects related to planning, implementation, procedures, financing, quality, control and supervision.
5. education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c is carried out in accordance with laws and regulations.
6. Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d is carried out regularly every 3 (three) months.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 30

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

So that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Sleman Regency.

Enacted in Sleman on 22 May 2017

heading: ELUCIDATION
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SLEMAN REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in such acts of violence. This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through the empowerment of women and optimization of the potential they already possess, so that they are expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community service is the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this, in order to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence and for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Paragraph (3) What is meant by "related parties" includes among others:
a. implementation of counseling in the legal field involving the police, prosecutors, district courts, religious courts, legal advocacy institutions and non-governmental organizations;
b. implementation of counseling in the health field involving the health office, regional general hospitals, and other health services;

heading: Article 22
translated_text:
Article 22

Paragraph (1) Point a What is meant by "medical services" is a form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.

Point b What is meant by "medicolegal services" is treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

Point c What is meant by "psychosocial services" is services provided by assistants in the context of traumatic recovery of the victim's condition including the provision of space and safe houses to protect victims from threats and intimidation.

Point d What is meant by "legal services" is services to victims in undergoing legal processes.

Point e What is meant by "social reintegration" is an effort to reunite victims with family members, substitute families/institutions, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

Point f What is meant by "economic independence services" is services for skills training and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.
